 The week in the news: Local, state and federal Election Day results; Paraguay’s president impeached
 Top local, global stories from Nov. 2-8 
 By Anoushka Chakravarty and Brianna Wang 
 • 
 Nov 8, 2026 
 Sam Rink A voter uses an electronic machine to cast a ballot in Latzer Hall at the University YMCA on Nov. 3, 2026. Voters make their choices on these machines, which then print those choices onto paper ballots that they turn in with the hand-written ballots. 
 On campus: Students vote on campus during midterms   
 Long lines at polling places on campus did not deter students from casting their ballots on Election Day. Those The Daily Illini spoke to mentioned affordability and immigration as some of their top priorities for this election cycle. 
 Liam Fazzi, junior in Business, was still waiting in line to vote at Siebel Center for Design an hour after polls closed.  
 “I’m especially excited about more young people getting involved in this stuff,” Fazzi said. “We the people are fed the f— up.”  
 In CU: CU election results   
 Democrat Nikki Budzinski , the incumbent U.S. Representative of Illinois’ 13th congressional district, defeated Republican challenger Jeff Wilson . The next term will be her third in Congress.  
 In Illinois House District 103, incumbent Democrat Carol Ammons won against Keith Smith , an independent candidate, to secure her seventh term in the Illinois State House of Representatives.  
 In House District 104, Democrat Mary Catherine Roberson defeated Republican incumbent Brandun Schweizer .  
 Democrat Dustin Heuerman , the incumbent Champaign County Sheriff, won against Republican Gregory Worrell . 
 Although the Champaign County Clerk race has yet to be officially called, incumbent Democrat Aaron Ammons leads Republican Alan Anderson 35,415 votes to 30,670 votes, as of Wednesday. Since Illinois accepts mail-in ballots postmarked before Election Day, official results may take time to be finalized. 
 In Illinois: JB Pritzker wins third term as governor, Juliana Stratton secures Senate seat 
 Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker won reelection Tuesday, defeating Republican Darren Bailey . The race was a rematch of their 2022 contest .  
 Pritzker is the first Democratic governor in Illinois history to win three terms. His running mate, Christian Mitchell , will become the next lieutenant governor.  
 Also on the ballot, Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the U.S. Senate race against Republican Don Tracy and will succeed longtime Democratic Sen. Dick Durbin to represent Illinois.   
 Stratton is the sixth Black woman to be elected to the Senate.  
 In the US: Democrats take House, Senate after midterms with historic victories 
 Democrats gained a majority in the House and Senate after weeks of campaigning and billions of dollars spent on both sides, total. Many states experienced significant wins, including Georgia, Texas, Michigan, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas and Maine.  
 Some of the notable victories include Georgia governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms , America’s first Black woman governor ; Adam Hamilton , Kansas’ first Democratic senator since 1932 ; senator-elect James Talarico and governor-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas, the Democrats’ first statewide wins since 1994 ; and Michigan’s senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, the country’s first Muslim senator .  
 In Alaska and Mississippi Senate races, Democrats Mary Peltola and Scott Colom hold narrow leads over their Republican and independent challengers. However, their races have not been called yet due to mail-in and absentee ballots and Alaska’s ranked-choice voting, as of Wednesday.  
 In the world: Paraguay Senate removes president after bank collapse; vice president sworn in   
 Former Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from his office Friday over his ties to the collapse of Ueno Bank , a digital lender, and he was taken into custody shortly afterward.  
 Prosecutors have charged him with breach of trust and influence for personal gain. Peña, who held shares in the bank’s parent company until last year, denies wrongdoing.  
 The 44 senators present voted to remove Peña, including members of his own party. Peña had offered to resign a day earlier, but senators impeached him instead, stripping him of the immunity former presidents normally have. The charges from the senate accuse him of conflicts of interest and misuse of pension money.  
 Paraguay’s central bank seized Ueno Bank on Tuesday, leaving more than half the country’s population without access to their accounts. An estimated 3 million depositors remain locked out. 
 Thousands of people protested the situation Thursday. Paraguayan currency, the guaraní, fell nearly 7% against the U.S. dollar this past week.  
 Pedro Alliana , Peña’s vice president, was sworn in as president Friday and is expected to serve through 2028. He promised that affected depositors “will be fully compensated.”

 About the Contributor 
 Sam Rink , Photo Editor 
 Hi! I’m Sam, and I am a senior studying journalism and gender and women’s studies. I started working at Illini Media Company in Fall 2023 as a staff photographer for The Illio, and I became the Senior Photographer for both The Illio and The Daily Illini in Spring 2024. Now, I’m the Photo Editor for both publications! Multimedia journalism is a huge passion of mine, so you might see my work in other publications around Champaign-Urbana.
